title: Refactor URL normalization edge handling

charges.claim: Removing the dot check in hasCustomProtocol causes URLs with dot-containing custom protocols to be returned unchanged instead of being normalized.

rebuttals.argument: The removed condition `!protocol.includes('.')` was incorrectly filtering out valid custom protocols like 'foo.bar:' that contain dots. The witness test expects such protocols to be treated as custom and thus normalized with the default protocol, which aligns with the function's purpose. The change correctly allows dot-containing protocols to be recognized as custom, enabling proper normalization.

rulings.reason: The change removes the dot check in hasCustomProtocol, causing URLs like 'foo.bar:baz' to be treated as custom protocols and returned unchanged instead of being normalized with the default protocol. The witness test demonstrates this regression by expecting 'foo:foo.bar:baz' but receiving 'foo.bar:baz'.

remedy.explanation: Restore the dot check in hasCustomProtocol to treat protocols containing a dot as non-custom, ensuring they get normalized by prepending the default protocol.
